small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=128, N=16384, K=16384 — M is tiny so most BLOCK_M=128 configs only spawn 1 row tile. Add configs with BLOCK_M=64/32 and larger BLOCK_N (256) with SPLIT_K=2/4/8 to expose more parallelism over the K axis; tune num_stages=4-5 for K=16384.
- The softmax kernel reloads x and bias three times per row over 16384 cols. Increase BLOCK_SIZE to 4096 or 8192 (cols are 16384, fits in 2-4 blocks) and use num_warps=16 to widen the row; consider a single-pass online softmax (Welford-style running max/sum) to halve global memory traffic.
- Fuse the bias add into the GEMM epilogue so the softmax kernel reads only one tensor (and skip the bias loads in passes 2/3); store gemm_out already biased.
large_guidance:
- Fuse GEMM + bias + softmax into a single persistent kernel: with M=128 rows, launch one program per row (or per row-tile), stream K in chunks computing the full N=16384 output row into registers/SRAM via an online (one-pass) softmax. Because N=16384 fits in ~64KB fp32, you can keep the row resident in shared memory and avoid the 3-pass reread entirely.
- Alternatively, since M=128 is small, treat the GEMM as a tall-skinny matvec-batch: persistent kernel over N-tiles, with each program computing a (128, BLOCK_N) tile by looping over K, then doing a grid-wide softmax via a two-stage launch (tile-local max/sum reduction, then normalize). This eliminates the separate softmax pass over the materialized GEMM output.
- Use fp16/bf16 tensor-core accumulation (cast weights once at init, cast x in-kernel) for the GEMM — 4090 has ~2x throughput on tensor cores at fp16, and K=16384 dominates runtime.
